findings.description: The bucket is intentionally public with no bucket policy or ACL restricting access, exposing all objects in the bucket to the internet. The associated object contains customer data (customer-master.xlsx), making this a data exposure risk.
The bucket has no server-side encryption configured, so objects stored in it are not encrypted at rest, exposing sensitive customer data if the underlying storage is compromised.
The object uploaded to the public data bucket stores customer-master.xlsx without any server-side encryption configured on the bucket, leaving sensitive customer data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no server-side encryption configured even though it is named financials and likely contains sensitive financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
The operations bucket has no server-side encryption configured, leaving operational data unencrypted at rest despite versioning being enabled.
The data_science bucket has no server-side encryption configured, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
